meta.rule: domains = intersection of the two blind labellers (none_cardiac if empty); domains_union = sensitivity; confidence = lower of two

labels.rationale_A: DOAC vs warfarin channelled by renal function, bleeding risk, frailty, cost and era; valvular AF exclusion minor.
labels.rationale_B: DOAC vs warfarin channelled by renal function, bleeding risk, cost/insurance, era; valvular/mitral stenosis to warfarin is a minor structural channel.

labels.rationale_A: Choice driven by renal function, dosing preference, bleeding history, insurance and prescriber habit rather than cardiac physiology.
labels.rationale_B: Same DOAC-vs-warfarin channelling: renal, bleeding, frailty, formulary, era; once-daily preference. Valvular AF minor cardiac channel.

labels.rationale_A: Dabigatran avoided in renal impairment, elderly, dyspepsia; cost and prescriber drive choice, not cardiac state.
labels.rationale_B: Dabigatran channelled strongly by renal function, dyspepsia, age/bleeding and formulary rather than cardiac physiology.

labels.rationale_A: Rhythm control chosen by AF burden, symptoms, LA size, LVH/CAD/HF (drug selection), baseline QT/conduction.
labels.rationale_B: Adding rhythm control driven by AF pattern/burden, symptoms, LA size, LV function and QT/conduction for drug selection.

labels.rationale_A: Ablation referral favours paroxysmal AF, smaller LA, younger, fit patients; drug-refractory rhythm; referral access also matters.
labels.rationale_B: Ablation referral favours paroxysmal AF, smaller LA, symptoms and prior AAD failure; also younger, fit, referral-centre access.

labels.rationale_A: Adding rhythm control depends on symptoms, AF persistence, LA size, structural disease, conduction and QT intervals.
labels.rationale_B: Rhythm vs rate control in elderly chosen by AF type/duration, symptoms, LA size, ventricular rate, LV function, conduction.

labels.rationale_A: In HF, rhythm control (amiodarone/dofetilide) chosen for tachycardia-mediated LV dysfunction, decompensation, QT/conduction status.
labels.rationale_B: In HF, rhythm control (amiodarone/dofetilide) driven by EF, AF-related decompensation, QT/conduction, LA size and congestion.

labels.rationale_A: Switching warfarin to DOAC in elderly driven by INR control, renal function, frailty, cost, patient preference.
labels.rationale_B: Switching elderly warfarin users to DOAC driven by INR lability, renal function, frailty, falls, patient preference and cost.

labels.rationale_A: Mainly surgeon preference and operation type; concomitant mitral surgery/Maze and LA enlargement partially increase LAA occlusion.
labels.rationale_B: Mainly surgeon/centre preference and operation type; concomitant mitral/maze surgery and LA enlargement give some structural channelling.

labels.rationale_A: Percutaneous LAA closure chosen for bleeding history, falls, OAC contraindication; cardiac anatomy secondary.
labels.rationale_B: Percutaneous LAA closure chosen for bleeding history, OAC contraindication, falls, patient preference; not ECG-reflected physiology.

labels.rationale_A: Ablation in HF selected by suspected tachycardiomyopathy, EF, LA size, AF persistence and electrophysiology referral.
labels.rationale_B: Ablation in HF chosen by suspected tachycardia-mediated LV dysfunction, AF type, LA size, symptoms; plus referral access.

labels.rationale_A: Clopidogrel instead of warfarin reflects bleeding risk, frailty, warfarin unsuitability, recent stenting; not cardiac physiology.
labels.rationale_B: Clopidogrel instead of warfarin in AF reflects OAC unsuitability (bleeding, falls, frailty) or coronary stenting; little ECG-physiology channelling.

labels.rationale_A: Carvedilol favoured in HFrEF/hypertension; metoprolol for AF rate control, post-MI, low BP, bronchospasm; partly prescriber habit.
labels.rationale_B: Carvedilol favoured in HFrEF; metoprolol for AF rate control, HFpEF, post-MI, COPD/asthma; heart rate and EF drive choice.

labels.rationale_A: ARNI switch targets confirmed reduced EF, persistent symptoms, cardiology care; cost, BP and renal function also matter.
labels.rationale_B: ARNI switch channelled to reduced EF, symptomatic/congested HF under cardiology; cost/insurance, BP and renal also important.

labels.rationale_A: Torsemide used for diuretic resistance and severe congestion, but institutional/prescriber preference and CKD strongly drive choice.
labels.rationale_B: Torsemide given for diuretic resistance, refractory oedema/gut congestion, advanced HF; but strong prescriber/institution and CKD effects.

labels.rationale_A: ARB over ACEi mostly reflects ACEi cough/angioedema intolerance and prescriber preference.
labels.rationale_B: ARB vs ACEi mainly reflects ACEi cough/angioedema intolerance, prescriber habit and formulary.

labels.rationale_A: In HF with T2D, SGLT2i chosen for HF benefit by cardiologists, tracking HF severity; eGFR and cost also important.
labels.rationale_B: Within T2D+HF, SGLT2i preferentially started by cardiology for HF severity/congestion; eGFR, age, frailty, cost also channel.

labels.rationale_A: Beta-blocker chosen for AF, tachycardia, CAD; avoided in bradycardia/AV block; ARB favoured in diabetes/renal disease.
labels.rationale_B: Beta-blocker chosen for AF/tachycardia, CAD/prior MI, HF; avoided in bradycardia/AV block; ARB favoured for LVH, diabetes.

labels.rationale_A: Amlodipine vs thiazide driven by gout, hyponatraemia, glucose, renal function, age and race; angina minor.
labels.rationale_B: Amlodipine vs thiazide driven by gout, hyponatraemia, diabetes, age, ethnicity, oedema; HF avoidance of amlodipine is minor.

labels.rationale_A: ARB favoured in diabetes, CKD, proteinuria; HF/LV dysfunction partially channels to ARB; amlodipine for older, angina.
labels.rationale_B: ARB vs amlodipine driven by diabetes, CKD/proteinuria, ethnicity, age; HF/LVH preference for ARB secondary.

labels.rationale_A: Beta-blocker channelled to AF, tachycardia, angina/post-MI, HF; avoided in bradycardia, AV block, asthma.
labels.rationale_B: Beta-blocker use driven by heart rate, AF, angina/prior MI, HF; avoided with bradycardia/conduction disease; amlodipine otherwise.

labels.rationale_A: Nifedipine vs thiazide driven by metabolic/electrolyte issues, renal function and prescriber habit; HF avoidance minor.
labels.rationale_B: Nifedipine vs thiazide driven by metabolic factors (gout, diabetes, electrolytes), age, ethnicity; angina minor channel.

labels.rationale_A: Mainly bleeding risk, age, OAC need, cost, PCI strategy; AF (needing OAC) and bradyarrhythmia partly favour clopidogrel.
labels.rationale_B: Mainly bleeding risk, age, invasive strategy, cost; concomitant OAC for AF favours clopidogrel, STEMI favours ticagrelor.

labels.rationale_A: Post-MI ARB vs ACEi choice reflects ACEi intolerance and prescriber preference.
labels.rationale_B: Post-MI ARB vs ACEi reflects ACEi intolerance and prescriber habit, not cardiac physiology.

labels.rationale_A: Driven by eGFR, glycaemia, cost, genital infection risk; prevalent HF partly channels toward SGLT2i in CVD patients.
labels.rationale_B: SGLT2i vs DPP-4i driven by eGFR, age/frailty, genital infection risk, cost; coexisting HF is a secondary cardiac channel.

labels.rationale_A: Linagliptin vs glimepiride driven by cost, hypoglycaemia risk, age and renal function.
labels.rationale_B: Linagliptin vs glimepiride driven by hypoglycaemia risk, age, renal function and cost.

labels.rationale_A: GLP-1RA chosen for obesity, glycaemic need, injection acceptance, insurance; DPP-4i for older frail patients.
labels.rationale_B: GLP-1RA vs DPP-4i driven by obesity, HbA1c, injection acceptance, GI tolerance, cost/insurance.

labels.rationale_A: Semaglutide channelled by BMI, weight goals, insurance coverage, GI tolerability, not cardiac physiology.
labels.rationale_B: GLP-1RA vs DPP-4i driven by BMI, glycaemia, injection acceptance, cost/insurance.

labels.rationale_A: Dulaglutide vs DPP-4i driven by obesity, HbA1c, cost, injection acceptance and frailty.
labels.rationale_B: Dulaglutide vs DPP-4i channelled by obesity, glycaemic need, injection acceptance and insurance.

labels.rationale_A: Mostly eGFR, glycaemia, cost and age; HF history partly channels to SGLT2i, relevant given HF outcome.
labels.rationale_B: Metabolic/renal/cost channelling dominates; prevalent HF favouring SGLT2i is a secondary cardiac channel.

labels.rationale_A: Canagliflozin chosen by eGFR, glycaemia, formulary; amputation/fracture concerns; cardiac physiology minor.
labels.rationale_B: SGLT2i vs DPP-4i driven by eGFR, amputation/PVD concerns, age, cost; HF minor channel.

labels.rationale_A: Sitagliptin vs sulfonylurea driven by cost, hypoglycaemia risk, age, renal function.
labels.rationale_B: Sitagliptin vs sulfonylurea driven by hypoglycaemia risk, age, renal function, cost.

labels.rationale_A: In CKD, linagliptin chosen for no renal dose adjustment and hypoglycaemia avoidance; renal, not cardiac.
labels.rationale_B: In CKD, linagliptin chosen for no renal dosing and hypoglycaemia avoidance vs cheap sulfonylurea.

labels.rationale_A: ARB vs ACEi reflects ACEi intolerance, prescriber and formulary factors.
labels.rationale_B: ARB vs ACEi driven by cough/intolerance, prescriber preference and formulary.

labels.rationale_A: Celecoxib vs naproxen driven by GI bleeding risk, rheumatologist preference, cost; CV risk minor.
labels.rationale_B: Celecoxib vs naproxen driven by GI bleeding risk, CV-risk perception, cost and rheumatology preference.

labels.rationale_A: Driven by cancer, renal function, cost, bleeding; massive PE with RV strain may get heparin-warfarin bridge.
labels.rationale_B: Apixaban vs warfarin in VTE driven by cancer, renal function, cost, era; massive PE/RV strain minor channel.

labels.rationale_A: Rosuvastatin vs atorvastatin largely formulary, cost, prescriber habit and drug interactions.
labels.rationale_B: Rosuvastatin vs atorvastatin choice is largely formulary, prescriber habit and drug interactions.

labels.rationale_A: Statin choice reflects intensity preference, LDL, interactions, prescriber/era; not cardiac physiology.
labels.rationale_B: Pravastatin chosen for frailty, drug interactions, statin intolerance, elderly; high-intensity atorvastatin standard post-ACS.
